submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole is a sparse, graded detector for the spatial or temporal setting of a situation: its peak falls on the preposition, motion/location predicate or date-clock expression that says where or when something is, goes or happens ('moved to the Canary Islands', 'staying in Kolkata', 'marching up from Saint Augustine', 'lived in', 'their attention elsewhere', 'moving toward the Internet', 'Friday (March 4)', 'meet at 8 P.M.', 'In 1881'), while abstract or evaluative statements with no such setting stay near zero. Peak size is carried by the setting rather than the entity: swapping one place, month or motion verb for another leaves the peak unchanged, whereas replacing the place with an abstract object, the location predicate with an activity verb, or the locative clause with a that-clause collapses it.

These guidelines apply to BA (Hons) Architecture and BA (Hons) Interior Architecture.
Architecture attracts a lot of applicants; we receive seven applications for each place. All applications at Northumbria University to the BA (Hons) Architecture course received before the January deadline will be considered.
We will not be holding interviews for this course. If you apply for BA (Hons) Architecture and meet our entry criteria will be asked to send in a selection of images from your portfolio and a decision about whether to offer you a place will be made by the Academic Team based on the quality of your portfolio. You should therefore ensure that the images you send us include what you consider to be your strongest work and should be chosen to demonstrate your abilities in a range of visual communication media that best displays your engagement with creativity and the design process. Please see below for advice on what to include in your portfolio. Applicants are advised to attend one of our Applicant Visitor days to see our excellent studios, facilities and to discuss the programme with staff.
Interior Architecture attracts a lot of applicants; we receive around five applications for each place. Our BA (Hons) Interior Architecture course encourages applicants straight from school, sixth form college and art & design foundation courses; applicants therefore apply at different times and all applications will be considered.
Interviews will be held for this course and we will contact you with an invitation to attend an interview event if you meet our selection criteria. The day will provide a general introduction, a tour of the facilities and a chance to meet and talk to current students. The interview is an informal discussion with, at least, one full-time member of the teaching staff and is an opportunity for you to get to know us and for us to meet you and learn about your work. You will require a portfolio for the interview, and advice on what to include can be found below. Applicants can also attend one of our Applicant Visitor days to discuss accommodation, studying at Northumbria and to see our excellent studios, facilities and to discuss the programme with staff.
Shortlisted international students who are unable to attend an interview in person will be interviewed via Skype.
Your portfolio will be a collection of your creative work and is a means for you to demonstrate both your abilities and your interests. We are particularly interested in seeing how you think and develop your ideas, so please bring sketchbooks and work in progress should be included. Your portfolio must include some freehand, observational studies that convey your interest in architecture and interior architecture.
Please note digital media on CDs/ DVDs/ memory sticks cannot be viewed during the interview.

If someone redefined undefined and it causes a problem - too bad! Some

drostie
> _Let 's say someone is using your library within that function and you
> reference undefined. You get the string "oops". Oops indeed._

That is incorrect. It might be correct if the word 'library' was replaced by
'code snippet' to indicate a copy-and-paste-of-your-code issue. But if you've
created a _library_ then your functions are over in some other file, where
`typeof undefined === "undefined"`.

The proper attitude here is the same as the Python attitude towards not having
`private` attributes: "If some other programmers want to do something crazy
with my code, that's their prerogative. If it blows up in their faces, that's
their problem."

work.

If `undefined` is an argument name, it's only bound inside that function and
nowhere else.

Yes, you can. You can also redefine __Array __, __Object __, and so on. If you
're writing a script to intentionally disrupt a system, __for(;;); __will also
do. This doesn 't happen in sane environments, so it really isn't a problem.

The Crockford quote (characteristically dogmatic, to the effect of ' _void

kicker.

O Movimento Passe Livre (MPL), que permanece acampado na Câmara Municipal de Salvador desde a última segunda-feira, 22, avalia na tarde desta quinta, 25, as propostas apresentadas pelo prefeito ACM Neto nesta manhã.
Durante a coletiva, Neto sugeriu duas medidas aos integrantes do movimento: bilhete único e a ampliação do domingo é meia, para quem utiliza o Salvador Card seja de meia passagem ou inteira. As principais bandeiras do grupo são a redução imediata da tarifa de ônibus e melhorias na mobilidade urbana.
O prefeito também informou que está à disposição para dialogar com o grupo, mas ressalta exceção para os partidários. "Eu dialogo com qualquer manifestante, mas aqueles que estiverem com interesse político-partidário como esse, eu não dialogo." enfatizou Neto.
Além de se posicionar sobre as medidas anunciadas pelo prefeito, o MPL também apontará as reivindicações e os rumos do movimento. Segundo um dos integrantes, o grupo vai desocupar a Câmara apenas quando o prefeito apresentar propostas mais concretas, em reunião com o Passe Livre. "As propostas são insuficientes, pois não apresentam nada do que nós reivindicamos", afirmou.
Entenda o caso
Em uma manifestação surpresa, 15 integrantes do Movimento Passe Livre (MPL) de Salvador ocuparam, na segunda, 22, a Câmara de Vereadores, a fim de pressionar os parlamentares para análise das reivindicações propostas pelo grupo na carta entregue ao prefeito ACM Neto.
Após um protesto na Assembleia Legislativa da Bahia (AL-BA) e na Governadoria, no CAB, na terça, 23, os manifestantes retornaram para a entrada da Câmara, conseguindo colocar mais nove pessoas para dentro do prédio.
Com três dias de ocupação, somente 16 manifestantes estão no local e pretendem permanecer até que o prefeito se reúna com o grupo para negociação.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The failure of large organizations is rarely dramatic. It is the slow accumulation of decisions that were reasonable when they were taken and were never examined again. A committee that has defended a procedure for a decade will usually defend it for another decade, not because the procedure works but because abandoning it would imply that the earlier decade was wasted. The same instinct shows up among university administrators, among hospital managers and among the executives of firms that have grown faster than their rules can absorb.

Reformers usually answer with a plan. A determined leader will appoint outsiders, rewrite the rules and set targets that expose the weakest links. Occasionally this works. More often the reform is absorbed by the culture it was meant to correct: the new vocabulary is adopted, the new forms are completed, and the underlying habits survive intact. The reason is not cynicism so much as self-protection. Nobody wants to be the person who admits that the report they signed was never read, or that the safeguards they endorsed were designed to be ignored.

A second explanation emphasizes incentives. If the reward structure favors process over outcome then process will dominate; if it favors blame avoidance then blame will be avoided at the expense of everything else. This explanation is powerful but incomplete. It treats incentives as fixed when in fact they are renegotiated continuously by the same people whose behavior they are supposed to explain. The circularity is uncomfortable, and that is precisely the point. Institutions are not machines that can be tuned by an outside engineer; they are agreements that hold for as long as enough participants find them tolerable. When enough participants stop finding them tolerable, the agreement does not collapse in an orderly way; it simply stops being enforced, and the paperwork continues to be filed by people who no longer believe in it.

The lesson, then, is about reversibility. A reform that depends on persuasion is fragile, because the argument can always be reopened. A reform that dismantles the machinery of the old arrangement is harder to undo, since restoring it would require effort that nobody wants to spend. The archives of a ministry are a good example. In 1953, the ministry transferred its records to a warehouse in Leiden, and the transfer became a model of irreversible change: once the files were beyond reach, the old procedures had nothing left to defend. Officials who had resisted the reform for years found themselves unable to argue for a system whose paperwork they could no longer produce.

None of this implies that outcomes improve. It implies only that some changes endure while others are quietly reversed. Whether the same trick can be repeated elsewhere is doubtful, because it depends on a coincidence of timing, money and indifference that is hard to arrange twice. The general point remains: arguments are cheap, and furniture is expensive.
